title: Algebraic Inequalities
tagline: Year 3 — Linear and quadratic inequalities, modulus, sign analysis and maximum-minimum reasoning

introduction.overview: An inequality asks for a range of values instead of a single value. The solving methods mirror those for equations, with one critical difference: multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign. This chapter covers linear inequalities, quadratic inequalities solved by sign analysis on the number line, modulus inequalities, and the quick AM-GM style bounds used in maximum and minimum questions.
introduction.placementRelevance: Range and "how many integers satisfy" questions are common in company aptitude rounds and in quant sections that test number sense.
introduction.realWorldContext: Budget limits, tolerance ranges in engineering and eligibility rules are all inequalities.

learningObjectives: Solve linear inequalities and flip the sign correctly
Solve quadratic inequalities with the number line
Handle |x − a| < b and |x − a| > b
Use AM ≥ GM for maximum and minimum questions

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: a < b means b − a is positive. Adding the same number to both sides keeps the sign. Multiplying by a positive keeps it; multiplying by a negative reverses it.

coreDefinitions: Linear inequality: ax + b < c with solution a ray such as x < k.
Quadratic inequality: (x − p)(x − q) < 0 holds between the roots; > 0 holds outside the roots (for p < q).
|x − a| < b means a − b < x < a + b (b > 0).
|x − a| > b means x < a − b or x > a + b.
AM-GM: for positive numbers, (a + b)/2 ≥ √(ab), with equality when a = b.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A quadratic with positive leading coefficient is a U-shaped curve. It is negative between its roots and positive outside them. Drawing the curve (or the sign line) answers every such question.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Move everything to one side, factorise, mark the roots on a number line, and read the sign of each region.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Sign flip
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Multiply or divide by a negative ⇒ reverse

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Quadratic, outside
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: (x − p)(x − q) > 0 ⇒ x < p or x > q

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Modulus
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: |x − a| < b ⇔ a − b < x < a + b

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: AM-GM
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: a + b ≥ 2√(ab); product max when a = b for fixed sum

mainNarrative: For a linear inequality, solve as an equation but flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative. From −2x < 6, dividing by −2 gives x > −3.
For a quadratic, factorise and use the number line. x² − 5x + 6 < 0 becomes (x − 2)(x − 3) < 0, so 2 < x < 3 and no integer satisfies it. The inequality x² − 5x + 6 > 0 holds for x < 2 or x > 3.
Modulus is distance. |x − 3| < 2 means x lies within 2 of 3, so 1 < x < 5, giving the integers 2, 3, 4. |x − 3| > 2 means x < 1 or x > 5.
To count integers, list the integers inside the interval and mind the open or closed ends. For −3 < x ≤ 4 the integers are −2 to 4, which is 7 integers.

For a fixed sum, the product is largest when the numbers are equal. If x + y = 10 with positive x and y, the maximum of xy is 25 at x = y = 5. For a fixed product, the sum is smallest when the numbers are equal.

deepDiveAspects.title: Never multiply by an unknown sign
deepDiveAspects.content: In x/(x − 2) > 1 do not cross-multiply blindly; move 1 across and combine to (2)/(x − 2) > 0, which gives x > 2.

deepDiveAspects.title: Endpoint check
deepDiveAspects.content: Strict inequality excludes the endpoint; ≤ or ≥ includes it. Roots of a denominator are always excluded.

solvedExamples.title: Quadratic
solvedExamples.question: Solve x² − 7x + 10 < 0 and list the integer solutions.

steps.title: Interval
steps.explanation: The product is negative between the roots: 2 < x < 5.

solvedExamples.title: Maximum product
solvedExamples.question: If x + y = 20 for positive x and y, what is the maximum value of xy?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: AM-GM equality occurs at x = y.

shortcutMethods.title: Number line

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Factorise, mark the roots, then alternate signs starting from + on the right (positive leading coefficient).

rulesForApplication: Equal split for the maximum product.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Test a value from each region of the number line.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Count integers carefully at the ends.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Many puzzle-style questions reduce to an interval and a count.
